column6:
The project title in URS LUDIP 2026-2035 and CALABARZON RDIP 2023-2028 is only "University Health and Wellness Center", different from the project title here in PIPOL.

A health and wellness center is a place where mental and medical healthcare professionals, nutritionists and life-coaches provide a variety of treatments and services for the health of their clients’ minds and bodies. An example is a free clinic found on college campuses that offer health screenings and general care to students and staff. Wellness is the pursuit of continued growth and balance in the seven dimensions of wellness. Many people think about "wellness" in terms of physical health only. The word invokes thoughts of nutrition, exercise, weight management, blood pressure, etc. Wellness, however, is much more than physical health. Wellness is a full integration of physical, mental and spiritual well-being. It is a complex interaction that leads to quality of life. With the student population of more than sixteen thousand students in a semester, a workforce of more than six hundred personnel and being the only state university in the Province of Rizal, it is much needed that prioritization of the health and wellness of its people be given of importance. The idea is to construct a three storey health and wellness center that will be open to the students, personnel and to the community which will be shared and inclusive as part of sustainable community thrust of the university.

column4: Implementation of the Comprehensive Action Plan on the Prevention of Adolescent Pregnancies Particularly Among Young Girls, pursuant to Executive Order No. 141, “Adopting as a National Priority the Implementation of Measure to Address the Root Causes of the Rising Number of Teenage Pregnancies, and Mobilizing Government Units for the Purpose”
column6:
In 2023, there were 3,343 babies born to mothers aged 10-14, a significant increase from 2,113 in 2020. Approximately 40 to 50 Filipino children aged 10-14 give birth every week. In 2022, the National Demographic and Health Survey (NDHS) reported a decline of 5.4 percent in adolescent pregnancy among 15-19-year-olds, down from 8.6 percent in 2017. This decline represents progress but still highlights the ongoing challenges surrounding adolescent pregnancies and emphasizes the need for continued efforts to address the issue. 

Cognizant of this situation, Executive Order No. 141 (June 25, 2021) was issued by the previous administration, which declared the implementation of measures addressing the root causes of the increasing number of adolescent pregnancies as a national priority. The Order specifically mandated the whole government to mobilize existing coordinative and legal mechanisms related to the prevention of adolescent pregnancies and to strengthen the capacity of adolescents to make autonomous and informed decisions about their reproductive and sexual health.

As specifically mandated under Section 5 of EO No. 141, s. 2021, the CPD will continue to educate leaders, parents, and community members to reduce, if not eliminate, adolescent pregnancy and improve adolescent reproductive health. Moreover, CPD was also mandated to consolidate a unified and harmonized action towards the prevention and reduction of adolescent pregnancies into a Comprehensive Action Plan. The Comprehensive Action Plan for the Prevention of Adolescent Pregnancy in the Philippines (CAP-PAP) for 2024-2028 is a consolidation of the key actions to be implemented by relevant government agencies and institutions.  As the Chairperson of the National Technical Working Group for the implementation of the EO No. 141, s. 2021, the CPD will spearhead the implementation of various initiatives to reduce and prevent adolescent pregnancies in the country.  

The proposed project aims to fund strategies and initiatives at the national, regional, and local levels.

column4: Philippines: Health System Resilience Project, Phase 1
column6:
The proposed project  aims to strengthen the Philippines' health system resilience, aligning with the government's health system transformation agenda. 

The project has four (4) components:
                                                                        
Component 1: Strengthening Provincial Health Systems - This component will support 17 selected provinces to strengthen primary care facilities (PCFs) and organizing them into primary care provider networks (PCPNs) linked with referral hospitals within the province-wide health systems (PWHSs). On one hand, the project will strengthen quality of care at the primary level, which is crucial for building trust in the newly established PCPNs. On the other hand, it will also enhance the capacity of district and provincial hospitals to ensure that patients referred by PCPNs receive quality and appropriate hospital care. In addition, the project will support  the enhancement of supply chain management.   
                                                                     
Component 2: Strengthening Health Emergency Prevention, Preparedness and Response (PPR) Systems - This component aims to enhance health emergency PPR by focusing on strengthening surveillance systems, laboratory networks, and emergency response. The project can also support such interventions at the national level in case of health emergencies.      
                                                                  
Component 3: Building an Enabling Environment, Project Management and Monitoring and Evaluation - Component 3 will support a range of activities to be implemented by the Department of Health (DOH). They aim to (i) strengthen DOH’s stewardship and institutional capacity, (ii) advance digital health transformation, (iii) enhance community engagement. This component will also finance project management  including project coordination, communication, procurement, financial management, social and environmental considerations and monitoring and evaluation (M&E) of the project.            
                                                            
Component 4: Contingent Emergency Response Component (zero allocation) - The CERC is embedded to strengthen the country's emergency preparedness and response. The CERC may be used following natural disasters or other crises and emergencies, allowing funds to be reallocated from other components of the project.

The Philippine Multisectoral Nutrition Project – Converging Nutrition Efforts for Our Children’s Tomorrow (PMNP-CONNECT) is the successor to the PMNP 1.0, designed to expand both the coverage areas and the range of interventions that address malnutrition across the country. Anchored on a whole-of-government approach, the project will be co-led by the Department of Health (DOH) and the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), with the National Nutrition Council (NNC) serving as the Steering Committee. This collaborative structure ensures stronger inter-agency coordination and alignment of national and local efforts toward improved nutrition outcomes.

PMNP-CONNECT aims to improve healthy behaviors and the simultaneous utilization of nutrition-specific and nutrition-sensitive interventions among targeted households. It focuses on promoting proper antenatal care for pregnant women, improving dietary diversity among young children, and ensuring the delivery of integrated health, nutrition, and social protection services. By building on the achievements of PMNP 1.0, the project seeks to institutionalize a sustainable, community-driven approach to reduce stunting and strengthen the foundations of human capital development in the Philippines.

column4: MOLECULAR AND CLINICAL APPROACHES IN AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER (Phase II): Project 1. The Reliability and Validity of the Childhood Autism Spectrum Test (CAST) in School Age Filipino Children
column6:
This project is under the priority area of neurodevelopmental research of the
Mental Health R&D Program, specifically the development and validation of
diagnostic tools appropriate for Filipino children with special needs. It is
expected to aid in the diagnosis and management of children with autism and
in the formulation of health policies and recommendations for addressing the
needs of the specified population.

Autism is a neurobehavioral and neuro-inflammatory disorder that presents as
core deficits in social communication and repetitive, ritualistic behavior. While
autism can be diagnosed at any age, it commonly manifests in school-age
children when the demands of the school environment exceed the capabilities
of the child.

Autism cases have been rising globally, yet there is a lack of information
regarding autism locally. This information gap prevents timely and adequate
responses from both government and non-government organizations and
affects the provision of services and proactive care for children with autism.
The current gold standard for diagnosing autism, ADOS-2, takes approximately
an hour to administer and requires a certified clinician/ specialist, limiting its
application in the community setting. Therefore, there is a need for locally
validated tools that will aid in the diagnosis of autism.

This study aims to validate the Childhood Autism Spectrum Test (CAST), an
autism-specific tool for school-age children. The CAST will be translated in
Filipino, Hiligaynon, and Bisaya and validated in these 3 languages. This is in
preparation for a prevalence study that will be done in the next phase.
The study's findings would allow for early intervention, referral, and support of
children with autism and would serve as a basis for health policies and
programs for this demographic.

column4: KALINGA Program: Development and Effectiveness Study of a Filipino Language App that Provides Anthropometric, Biochemical, Clinical, Developmental, Epigenetic, and hEaring (ABCDEE) Health Information, Monitoring, and Intervention Services Among Filipino Mother-Infant Dyads During the First 1000 Days: Project A - Improving Maternal and Child Health Services through the Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation of a Filipino Digital Health Application and Health Data Registry
column6: The first 1000 days of a child is considered a crucial window that may have a lasting effect on his or her future. Spanning roughly between conception up to the second birthday, this period is considered a window of opportunity to promote optimal health, growth, and neurodevelopment. Poor nutrition within this period has potentially long-term implications. According to UNICEF, poor nutrition in the first 1,000 days can cause irreversible damage to a child’s growth, which can lead to poor physical growth, diminished capacity to learn, and increased susceptibility to infection and diseases. (UNICEF, 2013) Since the ratification of Republic Act 11148 or the Kalusugan at Nutrisyon ng Mag-Nanay (First 1000 Days Act or “F1KD+”) in November 2018, the Philippines has made it a priority to scale up nutritional and health services with the goal of fostering health and well-being among mother-infant dyads. To support The First 1000 Days Act, many strategies should be explored to increase family participation, promote good health, and prevent child stunting. With the increasing popularity of web- and mobile-based platforms providing basic services to Filipinos, these same strategies should be seen as an opportunity to help Filipinos receive easy and affordable access to important health interventions. By providing timely alerts on nutrition, feeding and wellness, reminders for use of educational modules for patients, the Kalinga Program and its five component projects serve to act as a safeguard in terms of being able to provide Anthropometric, Biochemical, Clinical, Developmental, Epigenetic, and hEaring (ABCDEE) health information, and intervention services to mother-infant dyads. Through close monitoring, early interventions may be done, and proper referral systems can be tapped before the detrimental effects become permanent.

Long-term sustainability may also be affected if rainwater harvesting systems perform poorly or if water demand exceeds projections. Addressing these risks early is essential to ensure a reliable and sustainable campus water supply.

column4: MOLECULAR AND CLINICAL APPROACHES IN AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER (Phase II): Project 2. Molecular and Clinical Profile of Children with Autism Compared to their Age-Matched Peers
column6:
This project is under the priority area of neurodevelopmental research of the
Mental Health R&D Program, specifically the development and validation of
diagnostic tools appropriate for Filipino children with special needs. It is
expected to aid in the diagnosis and management of children with autism and
in the formulation of health policies and recommendations for addressing the
needs of the specified population.
Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition that
impairs people's ability to communicate and interact with others. Additionally,
ASD has been labeled as a neuro-inflammatory disorder. However, its etiology
and pathogenesis are still not completely understood.
Medical comorbidities commonly affect Individuals with autism. These include
micronutrient deficiencies, gastrointestinal problems, mitochondrial dysfunction,
thyroid problems, and mental health problems, among others. The study will
describe clinical findings and physical biomolecular markers that may herald
concomitant comorbidities of participants.
ASD has been recognized as a multifactorial illness with several genetic
causes, such as monogenic disorders, like fragile X syndrome (FXS), or
epigenetic changes, such as DNA methylation. The brain-gut-microbiome axis
is hypothesized to have a critical role in behavioral and medical symptoms
experienced by these individuals. The current study will investigate the gut
microbiome of children with ASD and compare it with their typically developing
siblings. Sequencing and bioinformatic analysis will be used to identify the
bacteria and fungi detected in stool samples as well as to obtain the children's
DNA sequences. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISA) will be used
to identify gut inflammatory indicators, including calprotectin, lactoferrin, and
secretory IgA, and these markers will be included as outcome measures.
The study will also assess the correlation between clinical manifestations of
ASD and physical markers and gut microbiome among children with autism.

column4: PHILIPPINE MULTISECTORAL NUTRITION PROJECT: CONVERGING NUTRITION EFFORTS FOR OUR CHILDREN’S TOMORROW (PMNP CONNECT)
column6:
The Philippine Multisectoral Nutrition Project Phase 2 (PMNP CONNECT) is a strategic national initiative jointly led by the Department of Health (DOH), the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), and the National Nutrition Council (NNC), with financial leadership from the Department of Finance (DOF). It is proposed for inclusion in the World Bank’s lending pipeline for Fiscal Year 2026, seeking a PHP 38 billion / USD 625 million loan through the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD). This significant investment represents the Philippine Government’s strengthened commitment to reducing malnutrition, improving human capital, and institutionalizing multisectoral nutrition systems nationwide.

PMNP CONNECT builds on the success and lessons from PMNP Phase 1, which is currently being implemented across 275 municipalities. Despite significant progress, the Philippines continues to face a high burden of childhood stunting driven by interlinked challenges in service delivery, supply chains, governance, financing, and information systems. In alignment with the Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition (PPAN) 2023–2028, PMNP CONNECT aims to expand its reach to 580 municipalities, including 80 municipalities in BARMM, covering all 34 priority provinces, and benefiting an estimated 10.2 million people—including approximately 5.8 million women of reproductive age and 4.4 million children under five.

At its core, PMNP CONNECT seeks to significantly reduce stunting prevalence across the Philippines by enhancing the simultaneous, adequate coverage of high-impact nutrition and health interventions during the first 1,000 days of life. Institutional leadership and implementation responsibilities are shared across DOH, DSWD, and NNC, with provincial and municipal governments serving as convergence integrators.

column4: Impact Evaluation of National and Local Strategies for Addressing Adolescent Pregnancy
column6:
Adolescent pregnancy continues to be a major public health and social development concern in the Philippines, with the country recording one of the highest adolescent birth rates in Southeast Asia. Early pregnancy often leads to interrupted education, heightened health risks for both mother and child, and long-term socioeconomic challenges that perpetuate cycles of poverty and vulnerability. Despite existing national policies and programs on adolescent reproductive health, the persistence of high rates underscores the need for more effective, context-sensitive interventions.

Local Government Units (LGUs) are uniquely positioned to respond to this issue, as they serve as the frontline implementers of health and social development initiatives. Their leadership and capacity to mobilize resources, engage communities, and integrate adolescent health priorities into local development plans make them critical actors in preventing child and adolescent pregnancy. Some LGUs have already demonstrated promising practices, but systematic evaluation is needed to determine which strategies yield measurable impact and can be scaled or replicated in other contexts.

This study seeks to conduct an impact evaluation of model LGU initiatives on adolescent pregnancy prevention, with the ultimate goal of generating actionable recommendations and designing a replicable initiative that can be adopted nationwide. By documenting outcomes, assessing effectiveness, and identifying enabling factors, the research will provide evidence-based insights to strengthen local leadership and inform policy advocacy. In doing so, the study aims to evaluate existing efforts and catalyze the development of a sustainable, community-driven initiative that protects young people’s rights, promotes their health, and contributes to inclusive growth.

column4: Upgrading of Lanao del Norte Provincial Hospital (LNPH) from Level I to Level III
column6:
The upgrading of Lanao del Norte Provincial Hospital (LNPH) into a Level III General Hospital, to be named the Lanao del Norte General Hospital, is a flagship health development initiative of the Provincial Government of Lanao del Norte. The project aims to transform LNPH from a basic Level I facility with limited services into a fully-equipped, specialized, and technologically advanced hospital that can serve as a provincial referral center for Northern Mindanao.

Currently operating with only a 100-bed capacity and facing chronic overutilization (140–200% occupancy rates), LNPH is under immense pressure to meet the growing and increasingly complex healthcare demands of the province. It lacks key infrastructure, medical equipment, and manpower resources required to deliver advanced, life-saving services. This project seeks to address those gaps and align with the national health agenda under the Universal Health Care (UHC) Act.

The proposed upgrade includes the construction of new hospital buildings, expansion of service departments, installation of cutting-edge medical equipment, hiring of specialized personnel, and integration of digital health systems. In addition, the project will institutionalize systems for emergency preparedness, disaster response, and ensure full compliance with the standards of the DOH for Level III hospital accreditation.

Once completed, the Lanao del Norte General Hospital will provide comprehensive tertiary care, including surgery, internal medicine, pediatrics, obstetrics and gynecology, intensive care, hemodialysis, imaging, and laboratory services. It will also serve as a training and referral hospital, enabling local access to specialized care that previously required travel to major urban centers.

In essence, this project is not just an infrastructure upgrade—it is a strategic transformation of the provincial healthcare system, ensuring equitable, quality, and accessible health services for all residents of Lanao del Norte and surrounding areas.

column4: Construction of 10-Storey Women's Health and Neonatal Care Specialty Center
column6:
The proposed Construction of the BRHMC 10-Storey Women’s Health and Neonatal Care Specialty Center aims to address the increasing demand for specialized maternal, gynecological, and neonatal healthcare services in the Bicol Region. As the only government hospital in Albay capable of managing high-risk pregnancies and complicated gynecological cases, BRHMC receives a high volume of critical referrals from both public and private health facilities. Its Neonatal Intensive Care Unit likewise caters to critically ill newborns from high-risk pregnancies and referral cases, underscoring the need for a dedicated specialty facility for mothers and newborns requiring advanced care.

The project involves the construction of a purpose-built, multi-storey facility equipped with modern diagnostic, surgical, and life-support equipment to enhance the hospital’s capacity to deliver timely, safe, and quality obstetric, gynecologic, and neonatal services, reduce referral delays, and improve health outcomes.

Gender and Development (GAD) principles are integrated into the project through the provision of gender-responsive facilities, dedicated breastfeeding areas, and a GAD and child-minding center. Patient support services will also be strengthened to ensure equitable access to specialized healthcare for indigenous peoples and underserved populations, reinforcing BRHMC’s commitment to inclusive and rights-based healthcare delivery.

column4: Equipping of Cancer Center Building of Western Visayas Medical Center
column6:
The Equipping of the Cancer Center Building of the Western Visayas Medical Center (WVMC) is a strategic health intervention designed to fully operationalize a specialized sub-national specialty center for oncology in Region VI. While the physical infrastructure of the facility is complete, its transition into a functional medical center requires the procurement and installation of advanced, high-precision medical technologies.

The core of this project is the acquisition of a Linear Accelerator with Stereotactic Radiosurgery (SRS) capability, which will allow for non-invasive, high-precision radiation treatment of complex tumors. Complementing this is the establishment of a state-of-the-art diagnostic imaging and nuclear medicine suite, featuring a PET Scan (Positron Emission Tomography) and SPECT-CT for precise cancer staging and metabolic imaging. Furthermore, the facility will be equipped with a 128-slice CT Scan for high-resolution diagnostic imaging and a DEXA Scan for comprehensive bone density monitoring, which is critical for patients undergoing long-term hormonal and systemic cancer therapies.

By integrating these specific technologies, the WVMC Cancer Center will provide a "One-Stop-Shop" for oncological services—ranging from early detection and precise staging to advanced radiotherapy. This initiative directly addresses the service gap in Western Visayas, reducing the need for patients to travel to Metro Manila for specialized care. Ultimately, this project fulfills the mandates of the National Integrated Cancer Control Act (NICCA) and the Universal Health Care (UHC) Law, ensuring that world-class cancer treatment is accessible, equitable, and affordable for the people of Region VI.
